item.title: Native IS Theories
item.content:encoded:
Varun Grover, University of Arkansas

Nik Rushdi Hassan, University of Minnesota Duluth

Tina Blegind Jensen, Copenhagen Business School

Paul Lowry, Virginia Tech

Kalle Lyytinen, Case Western Reserve University

Angsana Techatassanasoontorn, Auckland University of Technology

This special issue addresses the challenge of developing new theoretical frameworks to explain unprecedented digital phenomena reshaping organizations and society. The call emphasizes the need for native IS theories that combine new concepts with existing theoretical foundations to explain the "why" behind digital phenomena, moving beyond descriptive accounts to deeper theoretical understanding.

The issue welcomes both articles that critically engage with existing theories to demonstrate their limitations in explaining contemporary digital phenomena, and articles proposing novel native IS theories grounded in the IS discourse. Theories should contain logically interconnected propositions and address specific "why" questions about emerging phenomena like surveillance capitalism, artificial intelligence, social media impacts, and other disruptions requiring explanation.

Appel publié par European Journal of Information Systems. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Digital technology and its nexus with social and organizational phenomena
  • IT-enabled fake news and misinformation/disinformation
  • Algorithmic amplification and social tendencies
  • Cybersecurity and privacy threats from technology-enabled organizations
  • Deepfakes and synthetic media
  • Ethical and legal implications of emerging technologies
  • Artificial intelligence and generative content
  • Societal and political impacts of technology
  • Energy informatics and green IS
  • Sustainability digital initiatives
  • Digital strategy and emerging business models
  • Digital transformation and disruption
